children: In al engthy report published Thursday, Anthropic’s

Threat Intelligence team identified and disrupted numerous cases where “bad actors” exploited its AI models, including Claude Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus, for malicious purposes that ranged from fake dating apps to designing bioweapons.

The report covers activity between December 2025 and August 2026 across seven harm areas identified as cyber operations, influence operations, surveillance, scams and fraud, biological misuse, conventional weapons development, and distillation.
The culprits include Russian spies, Chinese hackers, and a Yemen-based weapons engineering cell, all of which challenged Anthropic’s
Once these threats were identified and disrupted, Anthropic
strengthened its safeguards and shared intelligence with authorities.

“Sophisticated and persistent threat actors continuously test our safeguards and try to circumvent the technical measures we use to detect and prevent misuse. We’ll continue to evolve our safeguards and coordinate with our partners to improve our ability to detect, disrupt, and prevent future misuse,” the company said in the report.

says that because of the sophistication of AI models, hackers can more easily exploit security vulnerabilities, “collapsing the labor and tooling gap that used to separate well-resourced, state-sponsored operations from individual operators.”

And although Claude is restricted in countries that include Russia, China, North Korea, and Iran, state-sponsored hackers were able to circumvent these restrictions and use AI models to research dangerous pathogens for bioweapons, spy on Ukrainian and European government officials, and develop weapons programs, including “kamikaze drones.”
